title: 2017 MAZDA MX-5 Miata

highlights: Low mileage (24,800 mi) with single-owner history
6-speed manual, desirable Soul Red Metallic color

normalized.prelim_summary: This 2017 Mazda MX-5 Miata Sport is a low-mileage, manual-transmission convertible in an attractive Soul Red Metallic finish, offered by a private seller in Napa, CA for $20,500. While the seller describes it as meticulously maintained with new tires and battery, the vehicle history report notes an accident or damage, which buyers should investigate further before purchase.

contradictions.detail: The description calls the car 'stunning, meticulously preserved', with 'showroom condition' and a 'flawless' top. The AutoCheck report on the same listing shows two minor collision/bumper damage events (12/2020, 09/2021), and the seller text omits them.

critical_evidence.evidence: AutoCheck shows dealer maintenance in 2019 and 11/2024, but has no reported entry from 07/2019 to 11/2024 (about 12k mi, 5+ years). No brake fluid flush is shown anywhere. The seller's 'freshly serviced, strictly maintained' is a sentence, not a receipt.

No transmission repair or warranty records. AutoCheck dates manufacture to 08/2017, which is later 2017 production and lowers but does not remove early-6MT risk. No door-jamb build-date photo was examined here.
The interior photo shows the floor mat in place and the top of the cabin looks clean. No lifted-carpet or behind-seat drain photos.

AutoCheck reports 'No Open Recalls', with recall service performed 06/2019, 07/2019 and 11/2024. The 11/2024 visit is likely the 24V695000 airbag software recall. Recall 19V072000 covers automatics only and does not apply.
Photos show Sailun Atrezzo SH408 tires with no legible DOT code, and a Super Start battery with a 12/25 sticker. There are no receipts for tires, battery or the 'fresh service'.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: VIN, clean title, single owner, odometer chain, smog pass and recall closure, all from AutoCheck. The maintenance half is incomplete. There is a 5-year reported-service gap, no brake fluid record, no receipts, and no repair documentation for two bumper events.

condition.rationale: Photos show a clean, stock car: tidy engine bay, good paint in the images, clean cabin and trunk, and a recently dated battery. Two minor bumper collisions are on record, and the underside, clutch, gearbox and cabin water areas are not examined here.

price_value.rationale: $20,500 sits at the bottom of the $20,590–$23,256 fair-value band. It is at the top of the profile's $17-20k band for a 2017 Sport, and two minor accident reports warrant a discount. Overall it is roughly fair, not a bargain.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual, low-risk Mazda, inside the ideal budget band, California-registered and easy to resell. ND1 power and base Sport trim are unremarkable but fit a bridge role. Availability is uncertain because a same-VIN listing was marked sold.

logistics.rationale: Napa is a day trip from Carmel, the car is CA-registered with a recent smog pass, and a local PPI is easy to arrange if the seller allows it. PPI access is not yet stated.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Soul Red with a 6MT, stock, single-owner is desirable. It is the base Sport with cloth seats, budget tires and an ND1 engine, with no Club/Brembo or GT content.

ppi_focus: Paint meter and panel-gap check on front and rear bumpers and adjacent fenders/hood for the two reported collision repairs; check bumper brackets and radiator support.
6MT shift quality warm and cold, especially 2nd/3rd synchros, plus pop-out under load.
Clutch engagement height and slip test in 4th-6th.
Footwells, seat-rail bolts and soft-top drains for water ingress or corrosion.
Soft-top fabric at the rear fold corners and header seal.
Water pump weep hole, coolant condition, valve cover and front crank seal seepage.
Rear differential pinion and output seals; underside for scrape or impact evidence.
Brake fluid moisture test and pad/rotor measurement.
Tire DOT dates and alignment check.
OBD scan for stored codes and confirmation of recall closure.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: bumper repair invoices plus a clean paint-meter PPI showing cosmetic-only work.
Up: dated receipts filling the 2019–2024 gap and showing a brake fluid flush, and tire DOT dates within the past year.
Down: PPI finds gearbox grinding, clutch slip, cabin water damage or poorly repaired bumper/structure.
Down: seller refuses a PPI or the car has already sold.
evidence.mission_note: A stock, single-owner, manual ND1 in California within the ideal budget band fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and should resell easily within 6-24 months. The open items are documentation, not mission conflicts.
evidence.rationale: The AutoCheck report verifies identity, a clean title, one Napa owner since 10/2017, an unbroken odometer chain, a CA smog pass in 11/2025 and closed recalls. It also shows two minor bumper collisions (12/2020, 09/2021) that the seller's 'flawless, showroom' description leaves out, with no repair documentation. Service history shows dealer visits clustered in 2019, then no reported entry for over five years until 11/2024. Absence in a report is not proof the work was skipped, but nothing shows a brake fluid flush on a 9-year-old car. Photos support a clean, stock car with a dated replacement battery. The 'premium' tires are a budget Sailun model with no legible date code. The August 2017 build date lowers early-6MT gearbox risk, though no transmission or clutch evidence exists. Price is at the bottom edge of the computed fair-value band, and the tracker shows a same-VIN listing marked sold on 2026-10-23, so availability is open.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller to confirm availability, then request the bumper repair invoices, tire DOT photos and consent to an independent PPI near Napa before any payment.
